In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Si application to sugarcane is an effective and environmentally benign IPM tactic for reducing stalk borer damage.
Si reduces the impact of N in promoting stalk borge (E. saccharina) infestation in sugarcane but not sugarcana thrips (F. serrata).
Si reduces the negative impact of N on E. saccharamia infestation but has no significant impact on the negative effect of N on F. serrata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of resistant varieties and Si nutrition can be effective in managing stalk borer infestation, while N nutrition is a potential management option for thrips.
Si application to sugarcane is a useful component of IPM for E. saccharia but not for F. serrata.
N and Si nutrition of sugarcane can be used to manipulate the impact of these two insect pests in different ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Si application can provide protection to sugarcane against the stalk borer E. saccharna but not the thrips F. serrata.
N fertilization can be used to increase sugarcane yields, but the risk of borer damage can be reduced through Si application.
N fertilization should be optimized for maximum yield and then Si nutrition should be used as an IPM option for reducing stalk damage from E. saccharana.
